# Parquet pushdown — in-browser perf sandbox

A focused A/B testbed for cold-start fetch performance against the canonical
S3 parquets via DuckDB-WASM. Goal: identify wins available **without**
re-baking the parquets — projection pushdown, predicate pushdown, metadata-only
queries, and httpfs cache effects. If the floor is "fetch the whole file
regardless", that's the diagnostic that justifies the rebake-and-promote path
from `2026-05-25_parquet-pushdown-sandbox.md`.

Two slow-loading datasets from the climateRationale notebook:

- `adm0_obs_periods` — CHIRPS+CHIRTS-ERA5 observational decadal stats (admin0).
  Dispatch flagged as ~69 s in browser; the historical pain point.
- `cmip6_2021-2040` — NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 ensemble season timeseries, one period
  parquet. Representative of the multi-file `parquet_scan([...])` pattern
  used in `dbFutureHive`.

## Setup

```{ojs}
import { patchWindowsCache } from "/helpers/data.js";
```

```{ojs}
// Two canonical S3 parquets to test. Add more by appending to this array.
perfTargets = [
  {
    key: "adm0_obs_periods",
    url: "s3://digital-atlas/domain=climate/type=observational/source=chirps-chirts-era5/region=africa/processing=admin-periods/variable=adm0_obs.parquet",
    cols: ["iso3", "variable", "period", "value"],
    isoCol: "iso3",
    sampleIso: "AGO"
  },
  {
    key: "cmip6_2021-2040",
    url: "s3://digital-atlas/domain=climate/type=hazard-indices/source=nex-gddp-cmip6/region=africa/processing=timeseries_mean_month/timeframe=3months/period=2021-2040/baseline=1995-2014/variable=ensemble_season_timeseries.parquet",
    cols: ["iso3", "scenario", "season", "year", "mean"],
    isoCol: "iso3",
    sampleIso: "AGO"
  }
];
```

```{ojs}
// Levers to compare. Each entry yields one row per target in the results
// table. `cacheBust: true` forces a unique URL so DuckDB's object cache
// can't serve a warm hit — this is how we get a real cold measurement.
// `pragmas` are SET statements run before the query.
perfLevers = [
  {
    key: "L1_cold_select_all",
    label: "Cold • SELECT *",
    cacheBust: true,
    pragmas: [
      "SET enable_object_cache = true",
      "SET enable_http_metadata_cache = true"
    ],
    query: (t, url) => `SELECT * FROM read_parquet('${url}') LIMIT 1000000`
  },
  {
    key: "L2_cold_select_cols",
    label: "Cold • projection pushdown",
    cacheBust: true,
    pragmas: [
      "SET enable_object_cache = true",
      "SET enable_http_metadata_cache = true"
    ],
    query: (t, url) =>
      `SELECT ${t.cols.join(", ")} FROM read_parquet('${url}')`
  },
  {
    key: "L3_cold_cols_predicate",
    label: "Cold • projection + predicate",
    cacheBust: true,
    pragmas: [
      "SET enable_object_cache = true",
      "SET enable_http_metadata_cache = true"
    ],
    query: (t, url) =>
      `SELECT ${t.cols.join(", ")} FROM read_parquet('${url}') WHERE ${t.isoCol} = '${t.sampleIso}'`
  },
  {
    key: "L4_cold_metadata_only",
    label: "Cold • parquet_metadata()",
    cacheBust: true,
    pragmas: [
      "SET enable_object_cache = true",
      "SET enable_http_metadata_cache = true"
    ],
    query: (t, url) => `SELECT COUNT(*) AS row_groups FROM parquet_metadata('${url}')`
  },
  {
    key: "L5_warm_cols_predicate",
    label: "Warm • projection + predicate",
    cacheBust: false,
    pragmas: [
      "SET enable_object_cache = true",
      "SET enable_http_metadata_cache = true"
    ],
    query: (t, url) =>
      `SELECT ${t.cols.join(", ")} FROM read_parquet('${url}') WHERE ${t.isoCol} = '${t.sampleIso}'`
  }
];
```

```{ojs}
// One DuckDBClient for the whole sandbox session. Levers that need cold
// behaviour cache-bust the URL instead of recreating the client — recreating
// would also pay the WASM init cost, which isn't what we're measuring.
sandboxDb = await DuckDBClient.of();
```

## Runner

```{ojs}
viewof runNonce = Inputs.button([
  ["Run all", () => Date.now()],
  ["Re-run (new cache-bust)", () => Date.now()]
], { value: Date.now(), label: "Action" })
```

```{ojs}
perfResults = {
  // Re-runs when the button is clicked.
  runNonce;

  const rows = [];
  for (const target of perfTargets) {
    for (const lever of perfLevers) {
      const cb = lever.cacheBust ? `?cb=${runNonce}_${lever.key}` : "";
      const url = patchWindowsCache(target.url) + cb;

      // Apply pragmas (cheap; safe to repeat per lever).
      for (const p of lever.pragmas) {
        await sandboxDb.query(p);
      }

      const sql = lever.query(target, url);

      // Resource-timing snapshot before / after. Browsers route DuckDB-WASM's
      // httpfs through window.fetch, so resource-timing captures every range
      // request. We attribute any entry whose URL starts with the target URL
      // (sans cache-bust) to this query.
      const matchPrefix = target.url.replace(/^s3:\/\//, "https://").replace(
        /^https:\/\/digital-atlas\/?/,
        "https://digital-atlas.s3.amazonaws.com/"
      );
      const beforeCount = performance.getEntriesByType("resource").length;

      const t0 = performance.now();
      let rowsReturned = null;
      let errored = null;
      try {
        const resp = await sandboxDb.query(sql);
        // resp can be an Arrow table or array depending on DuckDBClient version.
        rowsReturned = (resp && typeof resp.length === "number")
          ? resp.length
          : (resp && resp.numRows) ?? null;
      } catch (e) {
        errored = String(e && e.message || e);
      }
      const t1 = performance.now();

      const entries = performance.getEntriesByType("resource").slice(beforeCount);
      const matched = entries.filter(
        (e) => e.name.includes(target.url.split("/").slice(-2).join("/").replace(/^variable=/, ""))
              || e.name.startsWith(matchPrefix)
      );
      const bytes = matched.reduce(
        (a, e) => a + (e.transferSize || e.encodedBodySize || 0),
        0
      );

      rows.push({
        target: target.key,
        lever: lever.label,
        leverKey: lever.key,
        query_ms: Math.round(t1 - t0),
        http_reqs: matched.length,
        http_bytes: bytes,
        rows_returned: rowsReturned,
        error: errored
      });
    }
  }
  return rows;
}
```

## Results

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(perfResults, {
  columns: ["target", "lever", "query_ms", "http_reqs", "http_bytes", "rows_returned", "error"],
  header: {
    target: "Target",
    lever: "Lever",
    query_ms: "Query (ms)",
    http_reqs: "HTTP reqs",
    http_bytes: "Bytes downloaded",
    rows_returned: "Rows",
    error: "Error"
  },
  format: {
    query_ms: (v) => v == null ? "—" : v.toLocaleString(),
    http_bytes: (v) => v == null ? "—" :
      v >= 1e6 ? `${(v / 1e6).toFixed(2)} MB`
        : v >= 1e3 ? `${(v / 1e3).toFixed(1)} KB`
        : `${v} B`,
    rows_returned: (v) => v == null ? "—" : v.toLocaleString()
  },
  width: { lever: 240, error: 220 }
})
```

## Read the table

- **L1 vs L2** — if `Bytes downloaded` drops sharply, projection pushdown
  is working; the parquet reader is fetching only the relevant column chunks.
  If it doesn't drop, DuckDB-WASM is fetching the whole file regardless and
  no SELECT-list tweak in the production notebook will help.
- **L2 vs L3** — if L3 fetches dramatically less than L2 (or completes faster),
  predicate pushdown is also working. This is the rare best-case path:
  pushdown alone solves the cold-start problem and the rebake isn't needed.
  If L3 ≈ L2, predicate pushdown is blocked — most likely cause is that the
  canonical parquet has one giant row group (no `min/max` stats per row group
  for the parquet reader to skip on), which is exactly what the rebake fixes.
- **L4** is the floor — what cold-start would cost if only metadata were
  fetched. Treat as a target for L3.
- **L5** is the warm second-touch reference. Shows how cheap repeat queries
  are once the object cache is populated. Production users get this on
  *anything but the first query*, so the cold-start pain is really an
  L1-vs-L4 gap.

## Verdict (hand-rolled)

Once the table is filled in, paste the cold L3/L1 ratio per target back into
the dispatch:

```
adm0_obs_periods : L1 = ___ms / ___MB   |  L3 = ___ms / ___KB   →  ___× speedup
cmip6_2021-2040  : L1 = ___ms / ___MB   |  L3 = ___ms / ___KB   →  ___× speedup
```

If L3 ≥ 5× faster than L1 on both, we can ship optimisation as a
notebook-side query-shape change and defer the rebake. If L3 < 2× faster
than L1, the rebake is the only remaining lever and STAGE C of the parent
dispatch becomes the path forward.

## Out of scope (this sandbox)

- Canonical-vs-rebake A/B against `s3://digital-atlas/sandbox/parquet-pushdown/`.
  Skipped until the pipeline-side STAGE C upload lands.
- Promotion commands (STAGE F). See parent dispatch.
- Multi-file `parquet_scan([...])` A/B. We test one period file from CMIP6;
  the UNION pattern in `dbFutureHive` would be a follow-up if pushdown works
  on the single file.
